changelog: v349: a stated entry is never retired by shape. WHERE IT WAS SEEN: staging, 2026-09-24 19:18:10 UTC, hosted package pinned to v347 (`48ddabdf`). The owner answered a `residences` landmark card; the hosted `landmark-record` job filed one source, `sources/landmarks/entry-5d5e93f00610650276f2f86a.md`, whose whole body is `{"address":"701 North Williams","domain":"residences","label":"701 North Williams"}` — and commit `398b85df` "Landmark: residences (Lifehug Cloud)" RETIRED ALL 30 EXISTING RESIDENCE ENTRIES with it. `state/landmarks.json` residences went 30 -> 1; 29 `sources/corrections/temporal-*.md` were filed, each "Supersede N temporal claim(s) … superseded by a later residences answer (landmarks_interaction.entry_superseded_by)" with `correction_scope: landmarks/residences`, 89 claims in all. The published projection went generation 152 -> 153: nodes 1190 -> 1161, unplaced 35 -> 117, open work items 45 -> 154. Every moment those stays had PLACED by containment — "Attended Longfellow Elementary", "Fell on a nail", "Marriage to Katie" (2007-08/2009-06), "Job at Boeing", "Graduation from MIT", the whole childhood-moves sequence — fell to unplaced and minted a card. Later residence answers ("dad's house" 19:58, "Fiegers' house") filed normally 1 -> 2 -> 3, so the wipe happened once: on the first substantive answer after the pin. A `work` answer at 19:03 and `partnerships` at 19:39 did not wipe their domains (22 -> 23, 3 -> 4). WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS, and it is not the release anybody suspected: NOTHING IN v343-v347 BROKE. Running `unreadable_fields` over the 30 real entries and the residences row under v278, v342, v343, v345, v346, v347 and v348 bytes returns the IDENTICAL answer at every one of them — `('link','nickname','ongoing','place_ref')` for 23 entries, `('link','ongoing','place_ref')` for 5, those four plus `note` for 2 — and `entry_superseded_by` returns True for 30 of 30 at every one of them. The defect is **v278** (`8030d26`, "E-L2c — ladder fields, organization roster, chain coverage/gaps/closure, the one chain chooser") meeting **v214** (`eb50e89`, the cross-entry rule). Before E-L2c, `validate_landmark` on a rich residence emitted `{address, city, domain, label, span}` and `unreadable_fields` returned `()`; after it the same value emits `{…, link, nickname, ongoing, place_ref}` — five descriptors added to the writer and declared to `NON_RUNG_FIELDS` not at all — and `unreadable_fields` returns four. v214's rule 3, "a clean record retires the collapsed aggregate", had been reading those four as the signature of a machine that had many entries and filed one for sixty-four releases, waiting only for a residences record lean enough to carry none of them itself. The owner's 2026-09-15 place-enriched import armed it; the 19:18 bare answer fired it. `work` and `partnerships` were spared for the only reason that matters: no entry of theirs carried a descriptor, so `unreadable_fields` was `()` on both sides and rule 3 could not fire at all. WHY THE GUARD DID NOT CATCH IT: the ladder-consistency guard exists for exactly this, and its probe (`tests/test_landmarks.py`, leg 4) is a hand-written `everything` dict that E-L2c never joined — so it never asked about the five fields, its pinned `UNREAD` set stayed at six `(domain, field)` pairs, and CI was green throughout. That is the recurring-defect doctrine's own failure mode: a centralized definition whose INPUTS are still a hand list. THE RULE (`landmarks_interaction.A_STATED_ENTRY_IS_NEVER_RETIRED_BY_SHAPE`). `entry_superseded_by` becomes a yes/no reading of the new `supersession_reason`, which names which leg fired (`SUPERSEDED_BY_NONE`, `SUPERSEDED_AS_TERMINAL`, `SUPERSEDED_AS_COLLAPSED`) — because the two SPOKEN legs are things the person said and carry no further guard, and the SHAPE leg is the one that needs them. (1) ONLY A DEMONSTRABLE AGGREGATE: `collapsed_aggregate_fields` replaces `unreadable_fields` at rule 3, and a field is evidence of a collapse only when it is one the domain's own writer never emits, or a `span` the domain has no rung for whose bounds STRADDLE a stretch — which is v214's live instance exactly (the founder's four children as one row with a span across all four birthdays) and which one child's own single-date span is not. The readable set is DERIVED, never listed: `writer_stored_fields` runs `validate_landmark` itself over `_writer_probe_value`, built from `_TEXT_CAPS`, the new `WRITER_DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS` and the row's ladder and from no hand list at all; `NON_RUNG_FIELDS` now reads `_TEXT_CAPS` minus `IDENTITY_FIELDS` rather than repeating three of its keys; and `validate_landmark` drops any field not in that same declaration, so writer and store cannot drift apart again. The pinned six-pair domain-agnostic slack is unchanged and is now REPRODUCED from the derived probe, which is the proof the two probes agree. (2) PROVENANCE OUTRANKS SHAPE: an entry with a promoted source of its own is never retired by rule 3, whatever its fields look like — every one of the thirty still had its `sources/landmarks/entry-*.md` on disk while the rule was deciding a machine had written it. The guard sits in `timeline.save_landmark`, the seat that can see the sources. (3) ONE ANSWER IS ONE ENTRY: a single substantive record whose shape rule would retire more than one prior entry retires NOTHING, and the refusal is spoken — `supersession_findings` returns a finding in `lint_landmark_reply`'s shape naming the count (`SUPERSESSION_FAN_OUT_LINT`; the declined-for-provenance one is `SUPERSESSION_STATED_LINT`), which `save_landmark` appends to an optional `findings` list (additive — every existing call site is byte-identical). A count is the only part of this incident a log could have shown anybody. A `none` is exempt and always will be: retiring the whole domain is what "I never served" means, so its fan-out is the point rather than a symptom. The record itself ALWAYS files — a rule that cannot decide what it retires is no reason to drop what the person said. THE VAULT REPAIR, as a package verb: `lifehug.py landmark-reinstate --domain <domain> [--since <ts>] [--until <ts>] [--reason …] --apply [--json]` (`landmark_projection.reinstate_domain` / `domain_supersessions` / `landmark_correction_scope`). Undo is a STATEMENT, never a delete, exactly as it is for a move: it files ONE `retract` correction scoped to the new `temporal_store.CORRECTION_CORRECTION_SCOPE` naming every supersession that stops standing (`reinstate_corrections`, `reinstated_correction_ids`) — one correction machine, now three kinds of target, beside the `ordering_constraint` scope `timeline-move-undo` already used. `_fold` resolves reinstatement as a SET before any mark is laid, so the index stays a function of the corrections on disk and not of the order they were read in, and a reinstatement's targets are correction ids that are never reported as unresolved claim ids. The superseded corrections keep every byte and every reason. NOTHING WRITES AN ENTRY — the entries come back because `state/landmarks.json` is a drawing and the sources behind it were never touched, which is the invariant the v225 flip established. It writes `sources/corrections/` and `state/` and nothing else; it is deterministic (targets selected and sorted by content, never by mtime); and it is idempotent twice over, since the correction's id is a digest of what it says and `domain_supersessions` excludes what a previous run reinstated — a second `--apply` reports nothing to do. A bare run writes nothing and prints the plan, because a verb that undoes corrections in bulk is one the person should read before it runs; the `--since` window is what keeps it surgical, since a domain may hold perfectly good supersessions from other days and a verb that reinstated those would be the same class of defect it exists to undo. MEASURED on a copy of the owner's staging vault (`/private/tmp/lifehug-rig`, head `ade14e675`; the original was never written to): `landmark-reinstate --domain residences --since 2026-09-24T19:17:00Z` selected exactly the 29 incident supersessions and 89 claims and nothing else; with `--apply`, residences drawn 3 -> 33 (the 30 restored plus the three later answers `701 North Williams`, `dad's house` and `Fiegers' house`, all kept), residence stays carrying a usable interval 0 -> 30, containment placements (`participation_span_applied`) 31 -> 61, unplaced 51 -> 32, open work items 76 -> 48, nodes 1203 -> 1233, projection generation 164 -> 165, ONE file written under `sources/corrections/`, every one of the 29 still on disk, and a second `--apply` printing "nothing to reinstate". `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` DOES NOT MOVE, and that is measured rather than asserted: on a second untouched copy of the same vault, `fold_active_index(full=True)` and `project_landmark_entries` produce byte-identical digests under v348 bytes and under v349 bytes (`051502547fae6bc0…`/`8be440073779618b…`, 2020 active claims both times), because a vault with no reinstatement has no reinstatement to resolve and every field the writer emits it already emitted. It stays at v347's `timeline-rules:16`; only the package version bumps. NOT THIS RELEASE'S DEFECT, and named so it is not mistaken for one: the `landmark_flip: … parked=6 codes=invalid_landmark_identity_kind` line on every hosted job is separate, stable and pre-existing. It is `temporal_claims._validated_landmark_identity_kind` refusing six records whose `landmark_identity_kind` annotation — attached by `landmark_projection.entry_claims` when a place's name ENUMERATES, which a label with commas does — lacks the deterministic import provenance ADR 0033 requires. Those six never acquired claims at all, which is the likeliest reason 29 corrections covered 30 entries. The wipe was rule 3 and nothing else. GUARDS: `tests/test_v349_a_stated_entry_is_never_retired_by_shape.py` (46 tests) — the thirty in their real field shapes (synthetic values; 23 with a nickname, 5 without, 2 with a note) against the real bare record, asserting the writer emits every field they carry, that none of them reads as a collapsed aggregate, and that the bare record retires none of them; the wipe REPRODUCED by monkeypatching `WRITER_DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS` back out of `NON_RUNG_FIELDS` and shown to be caught by rule 3's own narrowing anyway, so the two guards are proved independent; both spoken rules still firing (a `none` over all thirty, a substantive answer over a standing terminal, a skip still not an answer); v214's own collapsed-children row still retired and one child's single-date span still not; a field the writer never emits still retiring; the fan-out refusal at 1, 2 and the incident's own 30, with the count in the detail and a `none` exempt; the derived probe reproducing the pinned six-pair slack; an undeclared descriptor proved unable to reach the store; the provenance guard and the fan-out guard at `save_landmark` over a real flipped vault; the reinstate round trip (wipe -> plan writes nothing -> apply -> entries back), proved to touch no landmark source, idempotent over three runs, leaving every supersession on disk, writing only `sources/corrections/` and `state/`, leaving another domain's supersession and a January correction outside the window standing, and still allowing a NEW supersession afterwards; the fold proved order-independent by reversing correction discovery order; a reinstatement target proved never to be reported as an unresolved claim; an ordinary `retract` proved unchanged; and the CLI in both `--apply` and bare form plus its `DIRECT_MUTATION_COMMANDS` classification. A TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, and fixed here because it was leaking into the checkout: `tests/test_v79_timeline.py` loads private copies of `lifehug_core` and `timeline` through a `load()` helper that goes to real trouble NOT to clobber the shared `sys.modules` entry — and then three of its tests did exactly that (`sys.modules["timeline"] = tl`) and never restored it. Every LATER test in the same process that imported `timeline` lazily — which every `cmd_*` in `lifehug.py` does, inside the function — got that private module instead of the canonical one, so a `mock.patch` on the canonical `LANDMARKS_STORE` did not apply and `timeline.redraw_landmarks()` redrew the CHECKOUT: full-suite runs were leaving `state/landmarks.json` (empty `domains`) and `state/temporal_claims/` in the repo, and `tests/test_queue_convergence.py::test_a_vault_with_no_projection_retires_nothing` then read them and failed. It was found by bisecting a v349 CLI test that passed alone and failed only in the full suite, and it is fixed by a `_bind_private_timeline(self)` helper that registers an `addCleanup` restoring the previous entry — in BOTH files that carried the pattern, since `tests/test_v110_timeline_corroboration.py` copied it from v79's including the part that leaked. `tests/test_v349_*`'s own vault fixture pins `timeline._projection_vault_root` as well as `LANDMARKS_STORE` and asserts on every teardown that the checkout was not written, so the next escape fails a test instead of a later reader. Full local suite: 6627 tests, 6622 passed, 1 failed (the known macOS-only `test_file_answer_outer_queue_leaves_no_plaintext_temp`), 4 skipped, and the checkout clean afterwards. Ruff parity held: `landmarks_interaction.py`, `timeline.py`, `temporal_store.py` and `landmark_projection.py` match their v348 finding sets exactly (one genuinely new SIM114 on touched code was fixed), and `lifehug.py` gains only four more of the `PLC0415`/`RUF100` deferred-import pairs it already carries seventy of.
